My family has worked this land in Quzhou for three generations. I know this soil. I know this sky.

I will grow winter wheat and summer maize, the same as always. That is what this land is for. My son moved to Shijiazhuang years ago so I farm mostly alone now, maybe my wife helps with the lighter work. I cannot manage more than 8 mu anymore — my back gives me trouble. When I was young I farmed 20 mu.

For wheat I will buy the improved seeds from the village supply cooperative, the flat-stemmed kind everyone uses now. It does not fall over like the old tall wheat did. My father used to save seeds but I stopped that maybe 20 years ago. The cooperative seeds yield better.

For fertilizer I will put down the same as always — a good base dressing of diammonium phosphate before sowing, then urea at jointing stage. I cannot afford to be stingy with nitrogen or the grain will be thin and light. Water I will pump four times for wheat — before sowing, at overwintering, at jointing, and at heading. Without irrigation in Quzhou you have nothing.

For maize after the wheat harvest I will plant hybrid seeds directly into the stubble — no need to plow again, saves my back and saves diesel money. Summer rains help so I only pump twice. I will spray pesticide if I see armyworm or aphid.

I do not do soil tests. I go by what looks right and what my father taught me.
